A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiCoRe study and contain readable text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–D. Relocated and renumbered material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original event-detection experiments across six datasets, component and output-format ablations, efficiency measurements, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds uncertainty reporting and results from larger ACE and MAVEN evaluation samples.

M1.justification: The Dreamer–Grounder–Judge pipeline, FSM constraints, prompts, and trigger atomization rules are retained. The expanded Outlines implementation explanation in Section 3.2 documents the existing procedure rather than introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate event detection on MAVEN, FewEvent, ACE, GENIA, SPEED, and CASIE. The larger-sample experiments reuse ACE and MAVEN without introducing new tasks, domains, or test scenarios.

E2.justification: The prompting, transfer-learning, and reasoning comparator sets remain unchanged in corresponding experiments. The added larger-sample comparison uses the already evaluated MD and MS baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds separate 1,000-sample evaluations on ACE and MAVEN in Appendix C.3, supplementing the original 250-sample evaluations. Existing metrics and decoding settings remain unchanged. CASIE's 50-sample exception was already documented in v1 Appendix B.1.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3 adds a limited check that DiCoRe's advantage over MD and MS persists with larger evaluation samples. Existing component ablations, output-format comparisons, efficiency analyses, and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: v1 reports three-run averages without confidence intervals or significance tests. v2 Appendix C.2 and Table 10 introduce confidence intervals for Llama3-8B-Instruct on MAVEN, FewEvent, and ACE, and report a t-test with p < 0.01. The stated run count remains three; interval construction, confidence level, and detailed testing procedures are unspecified.

E6.justification: Matched existing result tables retain their values. New Table 11 reports, under the 1,000-sample protocol, ACE TC F1 of 38.3 for DiCoRe versus 28.6 for MD, and MAVEN TC F1 of 15.3 versus 11.1 for MS. These supplement rather than replace the original smaller-sample results.

T1.justification: Event and trigger definitions, constraints in Equations 1–3, and the pipeline's mathematical formulations remain unchanged. The expanded FSM explanation introduces no new theorem, proof, or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same training-free divergent-convergent framework and principal performance and efficiency claims. The added experiments support existing contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 5.1 newly makes the reasoning-demand explanation for larger gains on large event ontologies explicit. Sections 2 and 3.2 expand discussion of potential applications beyond event detection and customization to other structured outputs. The limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 3.2 newly specifies FSM module inputs, Outlines choice lists, and deterministic handling of single-option transitions. Existing hardware and decoding details remain. v1's explicit promise to release test splits is removed, while the code-release promise and URL are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds references concerning creative reasoning, cross-lingual projection, and other structured tasks, including MacGyver, GPT-NER, and SQuAD. These modestly broaden research positioning while retaining the original related-work discussion.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the FSM explanation, moves dataset documentation from Appendix B.1 into Section 4, simplifies Appendix B's subsection hierarchy, and adds acknowledgments and an affiliation update. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 10–11, moves dataset statistics from v1 Table 7 to main-text Table 3, and relocates existing tables and prompt figures. Their designs are largely retained. New Table 11 incorrectly carries a caption describing the output-format ablation.

improvement.justification: Relative to v1's three-run means, v2 adds uncertainty reporting and larger-sample validation, while clarifying FSM implementation. These provide a modest improvement in empirical support and technical transparency. The gains are limited by unspecified statistical procedures, Table 11's misleading caption, and removal of the explicit test-split release promise.
